  (spec §5.5): applied with the new project, an identity, or refused with
  the rule's own sentence. An enum and its doc, nothing else. It is an enum
  rather than a side channel so that a site which has not decided which
  answer it gives does not compile; the fourth possibility, a request that
  could not be read, stays the `Err(String)` beside it. Its `Identity` doc
  is also the one place that says which non-edits speak and which stay
  identities on purpose (spec §5.5, §11 #88).
- `edit.rs` — the op enum, `parse` and `apply`. **Its module doc IS the op
  table's SEMANTICS half** — what each op means, and what an absent
  optional argument means — where `op_table.rs` is the ARGUMENTS half;
  `app/Sources/ReelOps.swift`'s typed builders, `AgentCatalog*.swift`'s
  tools and spec §6 mirror the two together. `OP_NAMES` is re-exported from
  here, at the path it has always had. `parse` answers an `Envelope` — the
  op AND the envelope's `scope` — and `apply_op(&Op)` knows nothing about
  nests. The semantics table is the reason this file is over the size cap
  and stays exempt (below).
- `op_table.rs` — the op table as DATA (road map 7's D3): one `OpRow` per
  op and one `Argument` per argument — its name, its `Kind` (`Kind::Output`
  for `set_canvas`'s dynamic range, `Kind::Blending` for its blending),
  whether the
  decoder requires it and, for the few that have one, its `Bound` — and
  `OP_NAMES` as a projection of it, re-exported by
  `edit.rs` so no caller moved. A published interface, where the `Op` enum
  and the dispatch are its implementation. Its one reader in the crate is
  `op_schema.rs`, which carries the rows out through the FFI; the APP's
  reader is every one of the sixty-four op tools in the agent catalog,
  which print these rows instead of restating them. **A `Bound` is
  published only where the core REFUSES outside it** — `set_canvas`'s two
  dimensions, sourced from `edit_canvas.rs`'s own constants, and
  `add_graphic_clip`'s `width` and `height`, from `model_graphic.rs`'s, never
  retyped — and never where it CLAMPS, which is the app's to say in its
  prose. A row holds no prose, no semantics and no default spelled twice;
  `Kind` is closed (twenty-three kinds; `Texts`, a list of strings, is
  `set_action_end`'s `off`), carries each vocabulary's members, and has exactly ONE
  kind per answer serde gives, because a distinction the
  decoder cannot see is one no test could prove. Nothing here is the
  authority — the enum's fields are, and `core/tests/op_table.rs` proves
  every row by asking the decoder. Capped at 400 lines like any new module:
  it does NOT inherit `edit.rs`'s table exemption.
- `op_schema.rs` — `op_table.rs` written as JSON Schema, which is what
  `rc_op_schemas` publishes (road map 7's D3·2): one object per op, its
  properties the arguments and its `required` the ones the decoder will not
  do without. **The match over `Kind` is exhaustive** — a kind added to the
  table does not compile until this says what JSON it is — and it is a
  module of its own because a row changes when an OP does and this changes
  when the published DIALECT does. It says nothing about what an argument is
  FOR (the catalog's prose), nothing about what a patch may CARRY
  (`Kind::Object` is an object with no properties; D1 left the core the one
  validator of that), and nothing about `additionalProperties` on an op,
  because the catalog merges `project` and `scope` in afterwards. Tested
  through the FFI in `core/tests/op_schemas.rs`.

  VIEW project from the nest (its tracks and clips at top level, its frozen
  size as the canvas, the parent's rate, media, `next_id` and nests, no
  markers), applies the op to it UNCHANGED, merges back. So `Project::clip`
  keeps its one meaning and no op has a nest-aware branch. Three things are
  counter-intuitive and measured: the scoped nest's own row stays in the view
  with its tracks and clips EMPTIED (removing it dangles every other nest's
  reference; leaving it whole doubles every id under `validate`); the nests
  write-back is union first, orphans after; and **a scoped apply has a wider
  `Err` arm than any unscoped op** — `check_caps` and `check_nesting` are
  document-wide and run on the MERGED parent, so an op valid inside the nest
  can still return `Err`. `refused_inside` is an EXHAUSTIVE match over every
  op, so a new op does not compile until it is classified. The READ half is
  `rc_project_scoped` in `ffi.rs`, which calls the same `scoped_view`.

  limit, answer its bytes; the twelfth `rc_graphic_library_usage`, G-46: the
  font files and assets the library's draws used; two re-exported from
  `ffi_graphic_pending.rs`)
  and the ONLY module of `core/src/` that names the `graphic` crate (spec
  §11 G-2; `core/tests/graphic_ffi.rs` reads `core/src/` to hold it). An
  `RcGraphicLibrary` is a BUILDER that the first compile or rasterize
  FREEZES into one `Arc<graphic::Library>` (the crate's `Library` is
  immutable — its `version` hashes every byte); an add after that is
  refused. `RcGraphic` wraps `graphic::Module`, whose `Arc` keeps the
  fonts alive past the library's free. `diag_out` is a JSON array of
  Diagnostics, exactly one error on failure; its panic arm goes through
  `ffi_util.rs`'s `fallible_op_wrapped`. `rc_graphic_library_families`
  answers the frozen library's family names as JSON — the engine's own,
  which a `font-family` must match (CoreText names 13 of 2500 host fonts
  differently) — and freezes it. `rc_graphic_describe` answers `{meta,
  schema, revision, warnings}`, `warnings` being `Module::warnings()`
  through `Diagnostic::to_json` (spec §11 G-24 (a)). G6 phase 5's toll T1
  moved the crate-free builder half to `ffi_graphic_pending.rs`
  (core-file-history); what is left names the crate (`diag_json`/
  `diag_error` name `Diagnostic`). `ffi_util.rs` holds the two crate-free helpers it gave up:
  `read_bytes` (a pointer and a length into an owned `Vec`, `bytes is NULL`
  refused) and `free_boxed` (drops a handle `boxed` made, under
  `fallible_op` with no channel; NULL a no-op).
- `ffi_graphic_pending.rs` — the library builder's crate-free half (G6
  phase 5's toll T1): `FROZEN`, `Pending`, `lock`, `rc_graphic_library_new`
  and `rc_graphic_library_add_asset`, `pub(crate)` for `ffi_graphic.rs`;
  it names no `graphic` item (G-2).

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit_clip.rs` and `edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

</system-reminder>

# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs`, re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,
  `Limiter` (format 30, spec §11 AU-21, written only when set) and `Duck`
  (with format 29's `DuckMode`, `pre_roll`, `hold` and `DUCK_SPEECH_PAD`)
  and `FadeShape` (`fade_in_shape` / `fade_out_shape`, and
  `Transition.audio_shape`), and their defaults, every format-29 key
  written only when not its default, and `AudioProps.isolation` (format
  31, spec §11 AU-50, 0…1, written only when not 0), and format 32's
  `Equalizer` (seven named slots — `HighPass`, `LowShelf`, `EqBand` × 3,
  `HighShelf`, `LowPass` — and `bypass`), `Hum` and `AudioChannels` (spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-34, each written only when set, `channels` only when not
  `both`), and format 33's `Gate` and `DeEsser` (`audio.gate`,
  `audio.de_esser`, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, after `channels`, each written only
  when set), and format 34's `Voice` (`audio.voice`, spec §11 AU-140, after
  `de_esser`, written only when set: a `VoiceKind` with no default, an
  `amount` defaulting to `VOICE_DEFAULT_AMOUNT`, an optional `pitch`; its
  ranges in `props_check.rs`, its clamp in `actions_clamp.rs`, the chains
  Swift's), and format 37's `Leveller` (`audio.leveller`, spec §11 AU-66:
  `target_db`, `max_up_db`, `max_down_db`, `response`, after `voice`, written
  only when set; its bounds `audio_dynamics.rs`'s); the FIELD `Clip.audio`
  stays in `model.rs`. Re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`; a pure move out of it (road map "audio" AP0), so the audio
  group's new keys land here.
- `audio_eq.rs` — the EQ's and the hum notch's bounds (format 32, spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-37): `check_eq` / `check_hum`, run by `props_check.rs`'s
  `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence (`audio.eq.<slot>.frequency
  must be between 20 and 20000, not 5`, a slope that is not 12 or 24, mains not
  50 or 60), and `clamp_eq` / `clamp_hum`, run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stage is Swift's.
- `audio_dynamics.rs` — the gate's, the de-esser's and the leveller's bounds
  (format 33, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, AU-46; format 37, AU-66): `check_gate` /
  `check_de_esser` / `check_leveller`, run by
  `props_check.rs`'s `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence
  (`audio.gate.ratio must be between 1 and 20, not 21`; times through
  `props_check.rs`'s `ticks_in_range`), `check_compressor` /
  `check_limiter` (under a prefix: `audio.` for the clip's, run by
  `check_audio`, and the track's own key for `track_dynamics.rs`, spec §11
  AU-150), and `clamp_gate` / `clamp_de_esser` / `clamp_leveller`
  (each field to its range, NaN to its default), run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stages are Swift's.
- `model_text.rs` · `model_shape.rs` · `model_regions.rs` · `model_motion.rs`
  — the text, shape, region and motion vocabularies, each re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`. Text and shape are the two sources the model only
  DESCRIBES and the platform draws and measures: nothing in either file is
  ever a measured size. Regions (`Spotlight`, `ObscureRegion`, `SpotShape`,
  `MAX_OBSCURE`) share one coordinate frame — the centre as an offset in
  SOURCE pixels from the centre of the layer's cropped rect — which
  `edit_zoom.rs` writes out as an equation and nothing else restates. The
  one load-bearing declaration order in these four is `ObscureKind`'s
  (`model_regions.rs`), a shader discriminant like `BlendMode`'s above;
  elsewhere only the JSON spelling of every variant is, so a rename needs a migration step. The enums are closed:
  there is no neutral kind to fall back to.
- `model_words.rs` — the word-caption vocabulary (format version 9, road
  map 8's W1b): `TextCase`, `Word`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill` and
  `WordStyle` (whose `template()` is what `patch.rs`'s text template walks
  against), re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELDS (`case`,
  `words`, `word_style`) close `TextProps`. Format version 12 (spec §11
  W-12) added three looks as KEYS, each off by default: `ActivePill.glide`,
  `WordStyle.active_fill` and `WordStyle.pause_dim` (0–1, range-checked in
  `props_check.rs`); `Word.end` is read by the recipe since then, not only
  by the pager. It also holds the two facts
  every writer of `text.words` shares, both `pub(crate)` and so named
  directly by their callers (a glob re-export cannot widen them):
  `token_count`, THE token rule (`split_whitespace` — the core is the one
  counter, spec §11 W-2), and `rebase_words`, the one saturating
  subtraction `trim_start`, `roll`, `add_transition`'s handle form and
  `split`'s second half make (W-3). Word times are clip-time POSITIONS: a
  negative start is legal, equal starts are legal, and `snap_animation`
  puts them on the grid after `check_text` has named what the caller sent.
- `model_graphic.rs` — the graphic vocabulary (format version 10, road
  map 10): `GraphicProps` (`name`, `width`, `height`, `in`, `length`,
  `props`) and `GRAPHIC_MIN_SIDE` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` and the schema limits
  `GRAPHIC_MAX_PROPS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_OPTIONS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_STRING` /
  `GRAPHIC_TYPES` (`GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` restates the engine's `MAX_SIDE` and the
  header's `RC_GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE`, and each other `GRAPHIC_<X>` the engine's
  `<X>`; `tests/graphic_ffi.rs`'s
  `one_max_side_in_the_engine_the_core_and_the_header` and its four
  `one_…_in_the_engine_and_the_core` tests pin them),
  re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELD `Clip.graphic` stays in
  `model.rs`. And the `pub(crate)` checks every writer shares: `check_name`
  (G-3's `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`, its clause `NAME_RULE` shared with
  `validate`), `check_side`, `check_schema` (the engine's sentences, COPIED —
  no module of the model may name the crate, G-2; a non-boolean `animate`
  on an entry is refused, G-41), `check_props` (by dotted
  path against the schema the op carries, shape only without one; a `null`
  is a removal and is never checked), `check_typed` (one value against its
  entry, answered normalised; `edit_action_graphic.rs` calls it under
  `graphic.props.<key>`), `check_count` (on the map about to be
  STORED). **A props map is changed only by `insert` and
  `shift_remove`**: under `preserve_order`, `Map::remove` is `swap_remove`,
  and `Project ==` cannot see the reorder.
- `model_look.rs` — the look vocabulary (spec §11 GR-7): `Look {kind, amount}`

  built-in looks' definitions as data — Color's four, Light's nine and a split

  the Camera Log of the media it converts, refusing first without

  the one check of a LUT named by media id, keyed by its field
  (`video.look.media`, `color.lut`).
- `model_media_color.rs` — camera log's vocabulary (format version 19,
  spec §11 GR-16): `LogCurve`, `CameraGamut` (`LogCurve::gamuts`, its
  default first) and `MediaColor` (`log`, `gamut`, `lut`, `detected`, and
  since format 22 `pq`, a `PqColor` — import's `file` reading, its
  `PeakSource`, the override `peak`, `PEAK_MIN`..`PEAK_MAX` — each written
  only when set; format 25 adds `canon_log2`, `canon_log3` and the gamut
  `cinema_gamut`, each Canon curve pairing with Cinema Gamut (its default)
  or BT.2020, spec §11 HD-17), re-exported by `model.rs` for `Media.color`.
  `media_color.rs` — its rules: `set_media_color` (a strict reader,
  `detected` and `pq` refused, its `peak` the override, "needs log or lut"
  judged on what the caller asked for, spec §11 HD-12),
  `check_media_color` (each refusal its own sentence; `add_media` and
  `validate` call it too; a `pq`-only colour stands), `without_camera_log`
  (what a LUT's removal or a paste leaves: the reading), `media_input` (the
  recipe layer's and the plan segment's `input`, with the effective `peak`)
  and `media_converted_by`.
- `dynamic_range.rs` — an HLG project's deliverables (spec §11 HD-5,
  HD-14): `DynamicRange` (`hlg`, `pq`, `sdr`), spelled `dynamic_range` both
  as an export override and as a recipe option; `deliverable` answers `None`
  for an audio row and for every row of an SDR project, else the picture:
  the six HDR rows (`hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `prores_422`, `prores_4444`) carry
  `hlg` (the default), `pq` or `sdr`, every other video row writes the SDR
  version, and `hlg`/`pq` are refused in an SDR project and on any other row, each in its own sentence.
- `av1_mp4.rs` · `ffi_av1.rs` — AV1 in MP4 (spec §11 CX-12, road map
  codec-export C1): `av1C` built from a full parse of the sequence header OBU,
  temporal delimiters stripped in place, and the `av01` brand put into `ftyp`
  (no `mp41` to replace is an error, never a file without `av01`); the three
  `rc_av1_*` exports. `leb128` is shared with `hdr10.rs`. The export table's
  `writer` field (`svt_av1` on `av1` and `av1_webm`; `avf_preset` stays the ImageIO
  switch) and the `encoder_speed` override (`faster` | `balanced` | `smaller`,
  refused on any other row) are `export_table.rs`' and `export_overrides.rs`';
  `Container` is `export_container.rs`'.
- `export_encoder.rs` — the bundled encoders' route and speeds (spec §11
  CX-12, CX-16): `Writer` (`svt_av1`, `libvpx`; none is AVFoundation; `takes_speed`
  false for libvpx's one speed) and `EncoderSpeed`, moved whole out of
  `export_table.rs` (codec-export C3's toll, a pure move) and re-exported there.
- `export_preset.rs` — `Preset`, its `impl` and `fps_json`, moved whole out of
  `export_table.rs` (codec-export C5's toll T1, a pure move) and re-exported there.
- `webm_ebml.rs` · `webm_layout.rs` · `webm_writer.rs` · `ffi_webm.rs` — the
  WebM an `av1_webm` or `vp9_webm` export writes (spec §11 CX-6, CX-15, CX-16: `V_VP9` with
  no CodecPrivate, BitsPerChannel 8 or 10; CX-17: `alpha_mode` on `V_VP9`, MaxBlockAdditionID
  and AlphaMode 1, `add_video_with_alpha`), the write side beside

  how much lies either side of it, and the one way a source in point moves.

  fits, and `window_of` / `overrun` (moved here from `edit_action_speed.rs`)
  are the fit test.

  clip's speed where the movers multiply by it: `content_length_in_source`,
  `last_in_point` and `last_still_time` answer in SOURCE ticks;

  with the clip's `start` among them, because a DURATION is measured from 0

  and `duration_at_speed` what

  `SourceBound` and not an `Option`,

  at all" to a transition: the three arms are `Unbounded` (a source with no
  window), `Unmeasured` (a media window that exists and cannot be measured)
  and `Timeline`, and a caller picks what `Unmeasured` means to it BY NAME,
  `or_unbounded` or `or_empty`. `in_advanced` / `source_advanced` is the one

  out of `model_query.rs` by road map 7 §10's phase A.

  `frames_back` (the grid position k frames before the frame nearest a
  position) and `frames_within` (the most whole frames back from a position

  property timings and finite positive speeds are outside this envelope.
- `outcome.rs` — `Outcome`, the THREE arms every edit answers with
  (spec §5.5): applied with the new project, an identity, or refused with
  the rule's own sentence. An enum and its doc, nothing else. It is an enum
  rather than a side channel so that a site which has not decided which
  answer it gives does not compile; the fourth possibility, a request that
  could not be read, stays the `Err(String)` beside it. Its `Identity` doc

  optional argument means — where `op_table.rs` is the ARGUMENTS half;

  tools and spec §6 mirror the two together. `OP_NAMES` is re-exported from

  op AND the envelope's `scope` — and `apply_op(&Op)` knows nothing about
  nests. The semantics table is the reason this file is over the size cap
  and stays exempt (below).

  op and one `Argument` per argument — its name, its `Kind` (`Kind::Output`
  for `set_canvas`'s dynamic range, `Kind::Blending` for its blending),
  whether the
  decoder requires it and, for the few that have one, its `Bound` — and
  `OP_NAMES` as a projection of it, re-exported by
  `edit.rs` so no caller moved. A published interface, where the `Op` enum
  and the dispatch are its implementation. Its one reader in the crate is
  `op_schema.rs`, which carries the rows out through the FFI; the APP's
  reader is every one of the sixty-four op tools in the agent catalog,
  which print these rows instead of restating them. **A `Bound` is
  published only where the core REFUSES outside it** — `set_canvas`'s two
  dimensions, sourced from `edit_canvas.rs`'s own constants, and
  `add_graphic_clip`'s `width` and `height`, from `model_graphic.rs`'s, never
  retyped — and never where it CLAMPS, which is the app's to say in its
  prose. A row holds no prose, no semantics and no default spelled twice;
  `Kind` is closed (twenty-three kinds; `Texts`, a list of strings, is
  `set_action_end`'s `off`), carries each vocabulary's members, and has exactly ONE
  kind per answer serde gives, because a distinction the
  decoder cannot see is one no test could prove. Nothing here is the
  authority — the enum's fields are, and `core/tests/op_table.rs` proves
  every row by asking the decoder. Capped at 400 lines like any new module:

- `op_schema.rs` — `op_table.rs` written as JSON Schema, which is what
  `rc_op_schemas` publishes (road map 7's D3·2): one object per op, its
  properties the arguments and its `required` the ones the decoder will not
  do without. **The match over `Kind` is exhaustive** — a kind added to the
  table does not compile until this says what JSON it is — and it is a
  module of its own because a row changes when an OP does and this changes
  when the published DIALECT does. It says nothing about what an argument is
  FOR (the catalog's prose), nothing about what a patch may CARRY
  (`Kind::Object` is an object with no properties; D1 left the core the one
  validator of that), and nothing about `additionalProperties` on an op,
  because the catalog merges `project` and `scope` in afterwards. Tested
  through the FFI in `core/tests/op_schemas.rs`.

  markers), applies the op to it UNCHANGED, merges back. So `Project::clip`

  counter-intuitive and measured: the scoped nest's own row stays in the view
  with its tracks and clips EMPTIED (removing it dangles every other nest's
  reference; leaving it whole doubles every id under `validate`); the nests

  op, so a new op does not compile until it is classified. The READ half is
  `rc_project_scoped` in `ffi.rs`, which calls the same `scoped_view`.

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit_clip.rs` and `edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

</system-reminder>

content.content:
### SW2a — the switch's planner and its numbers

- **What a person gets:** nothing visible: the planner that decides the cuts, its readings off the
  document, and defaults tuned on real speech.
- **Head (inside the phase, once the planner exists):** SW-S4 runs; SW-21's and SW-22's defaults
  recorded.
- **Decisions (draft):**
  - **SW-20 — The inputs.** Angles are tracks (SW-13): each track holding a selected media clip with
    pictures, two to nine. A microphone is a track: by default each track holding a selected sound
    clip whose MEDIA has no pictures; a camera's own sound counts only when no picture-less sound
    clip is selected (then each angle whose clips play sound is its own microphone); a camera's
    detached sound only when picked in the sheet's Microphone popup or named by the tool. Speakers
    are pairs of a microphone and an angle; by default a microphone that is itself an angle pairs
    with itself and the others pair, front to back, with the remaining angles; the wide is the one
    angle no microphone names, when exactly one is left. The range is the In/Out range, else the
    first selected angle clip's start to the last one's end. A microphone's steps outside its clips
    are silent. The switch trusts the placement and does not check sync (the guide says to run
    Synchronize Audio first).
  - **SW-21 — A microphone is active when its voice is its own.** On a 10 ms grid, for each
    microphone m: its level ℓ_m(k) is 10·log10 of the loudness cache's K-weighted mean square
    through the clip's channel matrix (AU-35) and source map, averaged over a CENTRED 100 ms window
    (k − 5 to k + 4); its voice v_m(k) the speech cache's probability for the 32 ms chunk at that
    step; P_m the 90th percentile of ℓ_m over v_m ≥ 0.5; F_m the 10th percentile over v_m < 0.5. m
    is active when v_m(k) ≥ 0.5, ℓ_m(k) ≥ P_m − `bleed_db` (15 dB) and ℓ_m(k) ≥ F_m + 6 dB; when two
    or more are active and one's ℓ − P exceeds every other's by `dominance_db` (8 dB), only it is.
    Provisional until SW-S4.
  - **SW-22 — Turns become shots.** One active microphone is that person, two or more crosstalk,
    none nobody. A turn bridges gaps under 0.5 s; a turn under `min_turn` (1.0 s) starts no shot;
    crosstalk of `crosstalk_min` (1.0 s) or more shows the wide, or holds the current shot without a
    wide or with `crosstalk: hold`; nobody holds the current shot; a shot starts `lead` (0.2 s)
    before the turn's first active step, frame-snapped; a shot whose angle does not cover its span
    goes to the wide when it covers, else extends the shot before; a shot under `min_shot` (2.0 s)
    merges into the one before (the first into the one after); the range opens on the wide when
    there is one; optional `wide_after` (off) cuts to the wide for `min_shot` once one person has
    held the screen that long.
  - **SW-24 — It refuses, naming every reason at once (SY-1's form):** fewer than two angles; a
    speaker without a microphone; one microphone for two or more speakers ("each person needs their
    own microphone" until SW8); a microphone whose loudness or speech is still being analysed; one
    with no speech found; a stretch no angle covers ("no angle has a picture between A and B"); a
    result past the clip ceiling ("Switch by Speaker would add N clips to M; the most is
    {RC_MAX_CLIPS} — raise the minimum shot", read from the header's define).
  - **SW-25 — The switch reads caches and computes nothing else;** the planner is a pure function in
    `SpeakerSwitch.swift`, probe-callable.
  - **SW-27 — The proof's speech is made on the Mac, its truth measured.** Samantha and Daniel (`say
    -v`) read a scripted turn table (skips by name without either); each voice's SOLO stem is
    written before mixing; each microphone is its speaker at 0 dB plus the other at a set bleed plus
    pink noise; a turn's onset is the first sample of its solo stem above −40 dBFS; a cut passes
    when on the frame grid and within τ of onset − `lead`, τ = 64 ms (two VAD chunks) + 50 ms (half
    the window) + one frame (about 147 ms at 30 fps).
- **Swift:** new `SpeakerSwitch.swift` (pure: SW-20's defaults and pairing, SW-21, SW-22, SW-24),
  `SpeakerSwitch+Read.swift` (readings off the document, AudioSync's `read`),
  `ClipLevelSeries.swift` (a clip's 10 ms level series through `ClipLoudness.ChannelMatrix` and its
  source map, the centred window); the generator `tools/proof/creator_spike/f_turns.py` (F-TURNS).
- **MCP:** none yet.
- **Docs:** SW-21's and SW-22's defaults and SW-S4's record here.
- **Acceptance:** `make gate`; SW-S4 recorded; the probe PASS.
- **Proof** (`switch_speaker_probe.swift`, scored by `switch_speaker_probe.py`): R1 SW-21 over
  synthetic series, each threshold at its edge, the centred window; R2 SW-22's turns, merges, lead
  and the hand-off to the wide; R3 SW-24's refusals as one list, the ceiling from `RC_MAX_CLIPS`; R4
  SW-20's defaults (picture-less files are the microphones; with none, each camera its own; a
  detached camera sound never a default); R5 a two-file angle covers its join, and a gap in every
  angle is refused naming it; R6 over F-TURNS' readings every cut within τ.
- **Mutants** (5): the bleed test removed (R1); the dominance test removed (R1); a trailing window
  (R6); a short shot merged into the next (R2); a camera's own sound taken beside picture-less files
  (R4).
- **Manual checks:** none. **Depends on:** SW1. **Lane** C.
- **Question for the owner:** the defaults (minimum shot 2 s, cut 0.2 s before speech, wide after 1
  s of crosstalk) as SW-S4 tunes them? *Recommended: yes.*

### SW3b — renders and Reverse read the clip's track

content.content:
placed per moment, and a track flag would catch every later clip on the track.

### TX7 — retakes, restarts and repeats

- **What a person gets:** the review also strikes an earlier take of a line said again, a phrase
  broken off and restarted, and a word or a few said twice in a row. Each strike names what it
  repeats ("An earlier take of 'So today we're going to…', kept at 02:14"); the last take is kept.
  No key is needed. "Find more with the Assistant…" puts a request for false starts that repeat
  nothing into the Assistant's message field for the person to send; it is greyed without an
  Anthropic key.
- **Head:** TX-70 (recorded at CJ0a) is checked to stand; TX-S4 runs; TX-71 records its setting.
- **Decisions (draft):**
  - **TX-71 — The retake rule's numbers.** A phrase ends at sentence punctuation, a pause of P s
    (voice cache) or a change of clip; a retake compares a phrase with the next K phrases within 30
    s, at a similarity θ (the longest common subsequence of normalised tokens over the earlier
    phrase's length) and a shortest phrase of four tokens; a restart needs an exact token prefix of
    at least two tokens, or the whole earlier phrase when it has one or two; a one-word repeat
    counts only when a pause separates the two words. Defaults before the spike: P 0.6, K 3, θ 0.6;
    TX-S4's rule sets them and may ship retakes off by default. The splitter is the shared one (CJ-8
    (j)), pure and parameterised, which FC4 calls.
  - **TX-72 — "Find more with the Assistant…" puts a request in the Assistant's message field and
    sends nothing:** "Find false starts in the transcript between <from> and <to> that repeat no
    words, tell me which words, then cut them." The button shows the Assistant tab; the person
    presses Return to spend. Without the Anthropic key it is disabled with
    `ModelKeys.sentence(.anthropic)` as its tooltip (CJ-12's Assistant row). No tool, no AI-7 row.
- **Swift:** new `RetakeFinder.swift` (pure: tokens, the phrase splitter, the three rules, chains
  kept last); `TranscriptReview.swift` (the three kinds); `AgentServer+TranscriptReview.swift`
  (`retakes`); `TranscriptBar+Review.swift` (the box and the hand-off);
  `EditorViewController+Assistant.swift` (`prefillAssistant(_:)`, showing the tab and setting the
  composer without sending); `AssistantView.swift` (the composer's setter); `AssistantPrompt.swift`
  (the false-start sentence, with TX-33's paragraph's Amended line).
- **MCP mirror:** `review_transcript {retakes}`. The hand-off is a person's button with no tool.
- **Docs:** `transcript.md`; `cleanup-tools.md` ("Cutting false starts with the assistant" says
  repeats are found in the tab); `assistant.md` (the hand-off); spec §4.3e; §11 TX-71, TX-72;
  `app/CLAUDE.md`.
- **Acceptance:** on the `say` twin of S-RT1 the pass meets TX-71's recall and strikes no trap word.
- **Proof** (`retake_probe.swift`, `retake_proof.py`, Release): Q1 the answer key on the `say` twin:
  every restart and repeat struck, retakes at TX-71's recall, no trap word; Q2 (probe, word lists) a
  chain of three keeps the last; fillers are ignored; different speakers are never compared; a
  retake across a clip boundary on one track is found; a duplicated clip and a hook copied to the
  open are never struck; Q3 `review_transcript {retakes: true}` equals the probe's items; Q4 the
  hand-off greyed with the Anthropic sentence with no key (`-RCSecretFolder` empty,
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` unset), and with the stand-in's dummy key it fills the composer and no turn
  starts; Q5 the pass runs with no key at all.
- **Mutants** (7): θ off by 0.1; the window at 1; keep-first; fillers counted as tokens; one-word
  repeats without the pause rule; different speakers compared; the same source compared with itself.
- **Manual checks:** **JOB-14** — retake strikes on S-TH1 and S-ST1: the kept take is the one
  wanted; a wrong strike is noted with its time. **JOB-15** — the hand-off with a real key: the
  Assistant names its cuts before cutting (as AS-10 checks).
- **Depends on:** TX6, CJ1; TX-S4 at its head (S-RT1). **Lane** A.
- **Questions for the owner:** (1) Retakes on by default? *Recommended: on if TX-S4's rule passes on
  your read, else off, with restarts and repeats on.* (2) The hand-off button? *Recommended: yes* —
  it costs nothing until you press Return.

**CU** (CU-S1…CU-S4 run in CU0b; rows whose grant is held by a launched `.app` run in a scratch
hardened-runtime bundle opened with `open -a`; rows that post input skip by name without
Accessibility for the poster, and the owner's one run covers them).

- **CU-S1 — Capture APIs, grants, clocks, the cursor's image.** Rows: A1 a listen-only `CGEventTap`
  (session) for mouse down/up, dragged and scroll, no grant; A2 the same tap for keys with no grant,
  Input Monitoring only, Accessibility only; A3 `NSEvent` global and local monitors, the same
  matrix; A4 `CGEvent(source: nil)?.location` polled at 120 Hz (µs per call, whether
  `CGWarpMouseCursorPosition` moves are seen); A5 `NSCursor.currentSystem` over TextEdit's text, a
  Safari link and a resize edge (identity, hot spot, reps, ms per call with a TIFF hash, the safe
  thread, whether it answers nil); A6 event timestamp against arrival `mach_absolute_time`, as ns,
  mach units and `systemUptime`; A7 keys delivered while the probe holds `EnableSecureEventInput()`;
  A8 whether the signed bundle needs a plist key or entitlement for ListenEvent, and whether a tap
  made before the grant works without a relaunch; A9 hidden cursors (a helper's `NSCursor.hide()`,
  TextEdit's `setHiddenUntilMouseMoves`): what `currentSystem`, its image and `CGCursorIsVisible()`
  report, 10 trials each; A10 a replacement for `currentSystem`: two 64 × 64 pt `SCStream`s around
  the pointer, `showsCursor` on and off, differenced, the silhouette's IoU against A5's image, 10
  trials over three cursors. **Rule:** positions are polled (A4) if a poll costs ≤ 20 µs median and
  sees warps and real moves, else they come from the click source; clicks and scrolls use the tap if
  it delivers ≥ 99 % of 200 events with no grant (Frame Job's own windows included), else the
  monitors if they do, else **STOP** (clicks not captured; the owner is asked before CU1a); keys use
  the tap under Input Monitoring alone, else the monitors, and if keys need Accessibility **STOP key
  capture** (CU6 is not built; the owner is asked); the image sampler asks at most 10 times a second
  plus once per mouse-down, `cursor_image=current-system` if A5 identifies another app's I-beam and
  pointing hand in ≥ 9 of 10 trials and its median cost × 10 Hz is ≤ 1 % of one core (≤ 1 ms a
  call), else `none` (no images; the cursor draws as Frame Job's arrow); whatever the verdict, every
  sample is checked for nil at run time, a nil records no change, and a segment whose every sample
  was nil writes `cursor_image: none` and says so on landing; hidden spans are recorded if a signal
  from A9 tells hidden from shown in ≥ 9 of 10 trials in both cases, else not (Hide when idle is the
  remedy); A10 is built only if A5 fails and its IoU is ≥ 0.9 in ≥ 9 of 10 trials
  (`image_fallback=a10`), else the arrow stands and an issue is filed with A10's numbers; the event
  clock is the hypothesis whose arrival − event lies in [0, 20 ms] for ≥ 99 % of events; secure
  input's delivered keys are noted, and the recorder drops keys under `IsSecureEventInputEnabled()`
  either way. Verdict line: `VERDICT positions=<poll|events> clicks=<tap|monitor|STOP>
  keys=<tap|monitor|STOP> cursor_image=<current-system|none> hidden=<recorded|not-recorded>
  image_fallback=<a10|arrow> event_clock=<ns|mach|uptime> secure=<withheld|delivered>
  relaunch=<needed|not-needed>`.
- **CU-S2 — From global points to movie pixels, and the time anchor.** In the picture: record with
  `showsCursor = true` over a flat-colour full-screen window, the burned tip found per decoded
  frame, the cursor warped along a known path, every frame's `SCStreamFrameInfo` and the polled
  samples logged. Separate's exact configuration (`showsCursor = false`, `showMouseClicks = false`,
  420v): the truth is the instrument's own 24 pt marker moved to the warped point at each step.
  Still start: the screen held still 2 s while the cursor moves, then a full-screen colour flip at a
  logged host time, recording which anchor the segment used and its error. Sources: a display at
  Nominal and at Best (2×); the instrument's window moved and resized; a window of odd size (1001 ×
  701 pt at 1×); a picked window; a second display when attached; each in both configurations.
  Candidates: **M1** `pixel = (p − screenRect.origin) × contentScale × pixelsPerPoint +
  contentRect.origin × pixelsPerPoint`, pixelsPerPoint the configured pixel width ÷ point width;
  **M2** M1 with `scaleFactor`; **M3** a fixed display frame from `SCDisplay.frame`; anchors E2, E1

    `keep` (the layer draws whole; its subject still hides Behind Subject clips, CO-50); `edge` −1…1
    shrinks or grows the outline; `feather` 0…1. Written only when set. Refused, each in its own

python3 - <<'EOF'
p='designs/creator-jobs.md'
s=open(p).read()
start=s.index("### CU3a — the cursor drawn as part of the layer")
end=s.index("### CO2b — masks made on demand")
new='''### CU3a — the cursor in the model, then drawn as part of the layer

CU3a is two pipelines (CJ-7's re-split): CU3a1 puts the cursor in the model and the recipe,
readable by agents and byte-identical for every project without one; CU3a2 draws it and makes
files wait for it. "CU3a" in a dependency means both. They share CU-30…CU-39.

- **Decisions (draft):**
  - **CU-30 — `media.cursor` and `video.cursor` (format p, CU3a1).** `MediaCursor {path,
    bookmark?, in_picture}` (`media.cursor`, written only when set) in `model_media.rs`;
    `CursorProps` (`video.cursor`, written only when set): `show` (true), `scale` (1, 0.25–8),
    `style` (`recorded` | `arrow`), `smoothing` (0, 0–1), `hide_idle` (null, or 0.5–30 s), `clicks`
    (`none` | `ripple`), `click_color` (`#ffffffcc`, G-25's grammar), `click_size` (1, 0.25–4).
    `scale` and `click_size` animate; `show`, `style`, `clicks` and `click_color` switch at an
    action's end; `smoothing` and `hide_idle` are the clip's — the recipe reads them from the BASE
    props, as `audio_track.rs` reads a base `audio.mono`, so no frame asks for a new smoothing (an
    end patch may carry them, CI-3 leaves the door, and they have no effect).
  - **CU-32 — The recipe's `cursor` key** (a layer's next key in landing order): `null` unless the
    clip's media has `media.cursor`, `in_picture` is false and `show` (or ripples) is on; otherwise
    `{media, at, reversed, smoothing, hide_idle, props}`, `at` the source tick in the stream the
    clip PLAYS (through S for a ramp, the held time for a still), `reversed` true when it plays
    reversed; Swift mirrors through `ReverseMirror` (D4-6).
  - **CU-33 — The composite inside `layerSample` before the grade (CU-4), at `texture(5)`** (CU3a2),
    the sprite lifted in an HLG project like any layer Frame Job draws (`LayerLift`), the ripple
    colour through `liftSDR`.
  - **CU-35 — An older project, and a media without a file, renders byte-identically.**
  - **CU-37 — A track not ready yet (CU3a2):** the preview draws without it and redraws on
    `.cursorTrackDidLand`; an export or `render_frame` waits; an unreadable or refused file is a
    `cursor_warnings` entry (each media once, the core's sentence) and the clip draws without a
    cursor.

#### CU3a1 — the cursor in the model and the recipe

- **What a person gets:** nothing drawn yet. An agent (or a proof) adds a media with a `cursor` in
  its `add_media` record, sets `video.cursor` with `set_video`, and reads both back through
  `get_project`; the recipe carries the `cursor` key CU3a2 draws. Every existing project is
  byte-identical.
- **Core:** `model_cursor.rs`; `cursor_props.rs` (`check_cursor`, `clamp_cursor`, one line each from
  `props_check.rs` and `actions_clamp.rs` after U5); `recipe_cursor.rs` (the key);
  `recipe_layer.rs`; `add_media`'s record carries `cursor`, and `relink_media`'s probe carries it as
  `original` is carried (the probe's value replaces the stored one); the format bump (`format.rs`,
  `format_history.rs`, `core/tests/schema_vN.rs`, the header's `#define`) — provisional, "(format
  p)" until it lands. `core/tests/cursor_recipe.rs` (the key's `at` through ×2, a ramp, a still and a
  reversed clip against an oracle; `smoothing` and `hide_idle` from the base at every time; `null`
  for `in_picture` and for `show: false` with no ripples; the refusals and clamps).
- **FFI:** the bump's `#define`; the key travels in the recipe JSON.
- **Swift:** `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaSnapshot` gain `cursor`; `VideoProps.swift` gains `cursor`
  (`CursorProps.swift`, a read-only mirror); `VideoPatch`; `RecipeLayer.cursor` decoded (not yet
  drawn).
- **MCP:** `set_video`'s description names the `cursor` keys (and that `smoothing`/`hide_idle` have
  no effect in an end); `get_project` shows `media.cursor` and `video.cursor`.
- **Docs:** spec §5.2a, §7.3; `core/CLAUDE.md` (`model_cursor.rs`, `cursor_props.rs`,
  `recipe_cursor.rs`, the layer's key count); `app/CLAUDE.md` (`CursorProps.swift`).
- **Acceptance:** core tests; the proof rows against Release; `make gate`.
- **Proof rows** (`cursor_layer_proof.py`'s first rows, Release; no grant): L1 `add_media` with a
  `cursor` and `set_video {cursor}` read back through `get_project`, a malformed `click_color` and a
  `scale` of 9 refused in their sentences; L3 a pre-CU recording's project before and after the
  bump: `get_project` and frames byte-identical; L9 an end naming `smoothing: 1` on a base of 0: the
  recipe's `smoothing` is 0 at every time (read through a probe of `ReelProject.recipeJSON`).
- **Mutants** (3): `in_picture` ignored (L3); `show: false` still keying ripples (core test);
  `smoothing` from the evaluated props (L9).
- **Manual checks:** none. **Depends on:** CU2, CU0a (U5), CJ0b (T2), CJ0d (T11, T14). **Lane** B.

#### CU3a2 — the cursor drawn, and files that wait for it

- **What a person gets:** a media whose cursor file says the picture has no cursor gets its cursor
  drawn by Frame Job, following every zoom and transform. Until CU3b only a media added with a
  `cursor` in its `add_media` record has one (an agent, a proof).
- **Swift:** `RecipeSource` publishes media cursor URLs beside the LUT URLs; new
  `Compositor+Cursor.swift` (mirrors `at` through `ReverseMirror` when `reversed`, pivot the media's
  model duration; asks `CursorTracks.ready` at the base smoothing, then `state`; binds the sprite
  and uniforms, or nothing until the track lands); `ReverseMirror.swift`'s doc gains its fourth
  reader; `Compositor.metal` (`layerSample` composites sprite and analytic ripples over the texel
  before `gradeSample`, behind one uniform-driven branch; every draw running `layerSample` binds
  `texture(5)`, a 1×1 placeholder when no cursor is drawn); `LayerUniforms` (groups of four in
  landing order: sprite rect, up to four ripples, ripple colour and size; Swift and Metal in one
  edit; the size proofs re-pinned as CO2a2 lists them); new `CursorSprites.swift` (image textures
  from `image` requests, once per image, lifted in HLG); new `Exporter+Cursor.swift` (an export or
  `render_frame` waits for every cursor track its range needs, `Exporter+RampAudio`'s shape, and
  publishes `cursorWarnings`). `MetalRenderer.swift`: no new pipeline.
- **MCP:** `render_frame` draws the cursor; `render_frame`, `export`'s answer and `export_status`
  gain `cursor_warnings` in `graphic_warnings`' shape (G-24 (c)).
- **Docs:** spec §7.5b; `app/CLAUDE.md` (the new files, `ReverseMirror`'s fourth reader, the uniform
  block's size); spec §7.9 (`cursor_warnings`).
- **Acceptance:** a project made over MCP with `add_media` (a `testsrc2` movie with no cursor and
  its fixture file) and `add_clip` draws its cursor at the file's positions; zoom actions carry it;
  the proof against Release; `make gate`.
- **Proof rows** (`cursor_layer_proof.py`'s drawing rows, and a probe through `MetalRenderer`;
  Release; no grant): L2 a 2× zoom: the cursor's canvas position equals (★) of its source position ≤
  1 px; L4 a ramped clip draws the cursor at S(clip time), a reversed one at `ReverseMirror`'s
  forward time, ≤ 1 px; L5 in HLG the cursor's pixel equals `liftSDR` of the sprite's; L6 export
  against `render_frame` at three times: identical; L7 cost against `show: false` with no ripples,
  median of 120 frames: ≤ 0.3 ms at 1920×1080 and ≤ 1 ms at 3840×2160 and 5120×2880 on the owner's
  Mac, no texture allocated per frame; L8 parity with a burned pointer (the sprite burned at the
  file's positions against the clean movie with the file, each with a blur filter, an obscure region
  over the pointer and a +1 exposure grade) ≤ 2/255 per channel; L10 an unreadable cursor file:
  `cursor_warnings` names it and the frame has no cursor; L11 with `-RCDevCursorLoadHold 2`, an
  export started at once draws the cursor in every frame.
- **Mutants** (5): `at` without S (L4); the reverse not mirrored (L4); the composite after
  `gradeSample` (L8); the HLG lift skipped (L5); the export not waiting (L11).
- **Manual checks:** none here (they need Separate recordings, CU3c).
- **Depends on:** CU3a1, CJ0d (T14). **Lane** B.

'''
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
input.description: Split CU3a into CU3a1 and CU3a2

    `offset` 0, A is extended into its handle by `L_t`; with `offset` above 0, a scratch copy of A
    is extended by `offset + L_t`, cut at `at + offset` by `split_clip`, and its second half (a
    fresh id) moved to start at `at`, so its `in`, base props and rebased actions are exactly what a
    ripple of the original's outer parts leaves; (3) when A and its linked partner both gain a
    piece, the pieces are linked by `pair_split_halves`' rule. The result equals the original with
    `[at, at + offset)` and `[at + offset + length, at + D)` rippled out, to the tick. Markers do
    not move. Locked tracks get nothing. A track with no cut at `at` gets a gap of `length` and its
    straddling clips (a music bed, a caption) keep every tick; a shorter cut is filled as far as it

    layout action of both roles, recognises it with `layout.rs`'s new pure `recognise(end, role,

action drops the planned action, counted. **`cursor_bursts.rs`:** typing stretches (marks under
  1.0 s apart, at least 3), shared with CU9b. **`action_class.rs`** (CJ-8 (i)), created here:
  `is_zoom` (the twin of `ActionBands.isZoom`), with `is_layout` and `moves` for CO6. The plan is
  answered as `remove_action` ops (Replace only), `set_video` ops (later bases), then
  `add_zoom_action` ops.
- **FFI:** none new (`plan_zooms` through `rc_cursor_query`, one track per clip).
- **Swift:** new `AutoZoomSheetController.swift`; new `EditorViewController+AutoZoom.swift`
  (validator: every selected clip's media has cursor data; passes the open nest's scope); the item
  in `AppDelegate+ClipMenus.swift` (153); the edit through `performGroupedEdit`.
- **MCP:** `auto_zoom {clip | clips, zoom?, lead?, stay?, follow?, typing?, replace?, from?, to?}`,
  `scope` declared, answering the actions added, replaced and dropped and the visits closed at a cut
  (`AgentServer+AutoZoom.swift`, a `creatorHandlers` row).
- **Docs:** `screen-recording.md` ("Auto Zoom"), `motion-and-transitions.md`,
  `menus-and-shortcuts.md`, `mcp.md`, the README highlight; spec §9, §7.9d; `core/CLAUDE.md`.
- **Decisions (draft):** **CU-70** the visit rules and defaults. **CU-71** the replace policy.
  **CU-72** typing's aim (CU-S3). **CU-73** the twin `is_zoom`. **CU-74** runs, the rest placement,
  and no transition across a cut. **CU-75** a placed clip refused; a nest's inside allowed.
- **Acceptance:** on a fixture with known clicks the plan equals the hand-made answer; on the
  owner's sample every click falls inside a zoomed region.
- **Proof rows:** Z1 5 clicks in 2 visits: 2 zoom-ins, 1 pan, 2 zoom backs at the stated times (core
  test and tool); Z2 the region clamped at a source corner; Z3 a ramped clip's actions placed
  through S; Z4 Replace off keeps a hand-made zoom and the overlapping plan is dropped and counted;
  Z5 (probe) `isZoom` and `is_zoom` agree on 12 fixture ends; Z6 undo removes every action in one
  step; Z7 a clip split mid-hold, Auto Zoom with Replace on the second half: its zoom back ends at
  the first half's base (±1e-6) and its base is reset to it; Z8 a visit across a run's cut places
  the picture identically either side (≤ 1 px) and no action straddles the cut; Z9 a screen placed
  side by side (scale half the fit) refused with CU-75's sentence, the same clip nested and planned
  inside with the nest clip's placement unchanged, and a screen at 1.2× the fit moved left planned;
  Z10 a reversed clip refused.
- **Mutants** (8): the merge gap ignored (Z1); the region not clamped (Z2); clip time without S
  (Z3); Replace removing non-zoom actions (Z4); the lead applied after the click (Z1); a later
  half's zoom back written as `region: null` (Z7); a transition straddling a cut (Z8); the placement
  check removed (Z9).
- **Manual check:** **JOB-25** — Auto Zoom on the owner's real tutorial: are the zooms where a
  person would put them? (A verdict carried into CU12.)
- **Depends on:** CU5, CU2. **Lane** B.
- **Question for the owner:** Replace's default? *Recommended: off*, keeping the person's zooms; the
  sheet says how many planned zooms were dropped.

- **What a person gets:** Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing… finds typing stretches with no speech and plays
  each at ×4 (the default), keeping 0.3 s at ×1 at each end. One undo step.
- **Core:** `cursor_typing.rs` (`plan_typing`): `cursor_bursts.rs`' stretches minus every speech
  span of the media playing under them (`media.speech`, or the speech cache Swift turns into it as
  `DuckSpeech.ops` does); a stretch never holds a shortcut nor the span of the overlay that follows

content.content:
### FC8a — Make Short from a range

- **What a person gets:** File ▸ Make Short from Range… asks for a folder, a caption style (a word
  style and look, or None), whether to cut filler words, and an Export row, then makes the In–Out
  range into a saved, captioned, filler-cut horizontal short queued on the Export Queue. No key.
- **Decisions (draft):**
  - **FC-80 — Make Short is, per span, in this order:** (1) the span into a new document through
    CJ5b's door (`display: false`), saved at its final path (FC-82), caches and graphics carried;
    (2) fillers: one `ripple_delete_ranges` of `FillerDetector`'s spans, "Remove Filler Words"; (3)
    the vertical step (FC-90); (4) captions: one `transcribe` with the chosen word style and
    `replace: true`, one engine per short — the clips named are the short's heard clips whose words
    FC-40 kept; `assemblyai` with `refresh` false only when every media behind them has a current
    carried transcript serving `.captions` (no request, with or without a key), else `apple` for
    all, the note saying why; (5) reverse: every reversed clip's backwards file present, else the
    short fails with "Clip N plays reversed and its backwards file is not rendered. Render it in the
    source (Clip tab ▸ Timing ▸ Render Reverse) and make the short again." (never queued to draw a
    slate); (6) save, queue the export, close. Fillers before the vertical step so the framing
    follows the final cut; captions after it so pages measure on the final canvas.
  - **FC-81 — Make Short never sends audio anywhere:** captions from a carried cloud transcript or

    block='\n'.join(sec[d:e])

    report.append((lines[a],jobs,'ADD'))
for r in report: print(r)
EOF

heads=[i for i,l in enumerate(lines) if re.match(r'^#{3,4} ',l)]
heads.append(len(lines))
edits=[]
for a,b in zip(heads,heads[1:]):
    sec=lines[a:b]
    text='\n'.join(sec)
    jobs=sorted(set(re.findall(r'\*\*(JOB-\d+)\*\*',text)), key=lambda x:int(x[4:]))
    if not jobs: continue
    di=[i for i,l in enumerate(sec) if l.startswith('- **Docs')]
    if not di: continue
    d=di[0]; e=d+1
    while e<len(sec) and sec[e].startswith('  '): e+=1
    block='\n'.join(sec[d:e])
    if 'manual-checks.md' in block: continue
    edits.append((a+e-1,jobs))
for last,jobs in reversed(edits):
    l=lines[last]
    assert l.endswith('.'), l
    add="; `docs/manual-checks.md` ("+", ".join(jobs)+")."
    if len(l)-1+len(add)<=100:
        lines[last]=l[:-1]+add
    else:
        lines[last]=l[:-1]+";"
        lines.insert(last+1,"  `docs/manual-checks.md` ("+", ".join(jobs)+").")
open(p,'w').write('\n'.join(lines))
print(len(edits))
EOF
